name: Ollama
tagline: Run models locally, with optional cloud models
description: Ollama is a tool for running large language models on your own hardware, with optional paid plans for cloud-hosted models. Its source code is published on GitHub under the MIT licence.
features: Runs models on your own hardware, which the FAQ says is always unlimited
useCases: Using cloud-hosted models without managing GPUs
strengths: Local use is unlimited and the GitHub repository is MIT-licensed
Free pay-as-you-go plan with pay-per-token cloud models
limitations: Cloud models are hosted primarily in the United States, with possible routing to Europe
Team is listed as early access

plans.name: Pay as you go
highlights: Pay per token for every cloud model

plans.name: Team (early access)
highlights: $1,000 usage credits per month shared across the team
limits: $1,000 of shared usage credits per month

plans.name: Enterprise
highlights: Cost budgets for users and API keys

free.details: Pay as you go is $0 per month with 3 concurrent requests and pay-per-token cloud models. Running models on your own hardware is always unlimited.

pricing.regional: Currency shown as '$' without a code. Tax treatment: not stated. Off-peak model pricing applies outside 12:00 to 18:00 UTC on weekdays and all day on weekends.

openSource.note: MIT licence shown on the GitHub repository

verification.notes: Product active. Pay as you go $0 (local models, 3 concurrent cloud requests); Pro $20/month or $200/year billed annually ($60 of monthly usage credits); Team early access $500/month ($1,000 of shared monthly credits, unlimited users); Enterprise custom. The Max tier price was not re-read.
verification.method: Opened in the Claude desktop built-in browser; page text read

profile.headline: Run open models on your own machine, or in the cloud, with a simple command line

capabilities.title: Run models locally or in the cloud
capabilities.text: Access the latest open models with complete privacy; the site says prompts are never stored or trained on.

capabilities.title: Chat with a model in one command
capabilities.text: Run a model from the Ollama library straight from the terminal.

capabilities.title: Connect coding tools
capabilities.text: Launch tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and OpenCode against your models.

capabilities.title: Build on a REST API
capabilities.text: Endpoints run and manage models, with Python and JavaScript client libraries.

featureCards.name: Launch integrations
featureCards.text: Start a coding tool with a single launch command.

featureCards.name: OpenClaw assistant
featureCards.text: An assistant that the README says can run across WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and Discord.

featureCards.name: Modelfile and importing
featureCards.text: Reference pages for importing and customising models.

featureCards.name: Open source
featureCards.text: The project is MIT-licensed and built on llama.cpp.

audienceDetail.text: The libraries, REST API and docs are written for people building applications. The pages do not name an audience, so these groups follow from what they document.

audienceDetail.who: People who want models to stay private
audienceDetail.text: Local running is the privacy argument the site makes.
Several coding tools can be pointed at local models.
